meta.name: CULL
meta.description: Four colours, one typeface, no ornament. Cream paper, teal ink, gold for neglect, terracotta for consequence. Every value here is enforced by a test. Do not hardcode a value in a widget; add it here and regenerate.

color._note: Cream paper, never white. Teal is the only 'good'. Gold is neglect, not warning. Terracotta is consequence. None of the three brand colours clears 4.5:1 as text on cream (teal 2.96, gold 1.48, terracotta 2.74), so they are fills, rules and accents only. Type on cream is always ink.

surface_4.role: Layer 4. The highest: sheets and dialogs. It is a visible step below the canvas, but it cannot go much further: the lightest ink that has to clear AA on it, signal_dim, is already at 4.77:1 here and drops under 4.5 by the next step down. A sheet floats on its border and its shadow, not on a large fill difference, so this is the right trade.

ink_primary.role: Headlines. A near-black with a teal cast, so it belongs to the palette.

ink_mono.role: Receipts: dates, domains, scores. Mono is truth.

ink_disabled.role: Disabled only. Never carries meaning alone.

ink_on_accent.role: Text on a teal, gold or terracotta fill. Darker than ink_primary, because those fills are mid-lightness.

ink_inverse.role: Text on ink. The only time cream is type.

signal.role: Teal. The only positive. Kept, fresh, done.

signal_dim.role: Teal for hairlines and text on cream, where the bright value is too light.

signal_deep.role: The deep teal. Focus rings, and the one place the app goes dark to be heard.

accent.role: Gold. Neglect. Stale, untouched, ageing well or badly.

accent_dim.role: Gold as text on cream, where the bright value cannot be read.

danger.role: Terracotta. Consequence. The cull, and the loudest honest moment.

danger_dim.role: Terracotta as text on cream, and the graveyard.

success.role: Restored, forged, kept. Teal's text-weight twin.

warn.role: Confirmations that stop you. Gold's text-weight twin.

focus.role: Focus ring. Always visible, never removed.

scrim.role: Behind sheets and the cull confirmation. Ink rather than black: dimming a warm page with neutral black reads as a dead grey screen, and this reads as lowering a lamp. At 0.55 the dimmed page sits 3.67:1 below the canvas, which is a visible separation without hiding what is behind it.

hoardBand._note: The guilt ramp. Every band carries two values, because the bright brand colour and the readable brand colour are not the same. 'value' is the fill, and it always takes ink_on_accent on top: gold as a fill is a pale wash with 10.65:1 under it. 'graphic' is the stroke, the dial arc, the bar, and anything drawn directly on cream, where the fill value would be 1.48:1 and invisible. Using the wrong one silently costs low-vision and colour-blind users the verdict.

category._note: Eight categories from three hues, so they are separated by luminance rather than by hue. The teal and the terracotta would otherwise collapse into each other for a deuteranope. The ceiling on `value` is 0.26 relative luminance: above that a swatch falls under 3:1 on the cream and becomes invisible, which is the failure that matters most here, because the swatch is the only colour cue on a card. The values step down evenly from 0.26 to 0.03, 0.033 apart, so no two are within 0.02 and none are distinguishable by brightness alone. Each one always ships with its label, so colour is never the only signal.

type._note: One family. Geist does the whole job: bold for the argument, regular for the receipts, mono for anything that is a fact. There is no serif, because a second voice would be a second argument.

display.note: Self-hosted. Bold is the default weight, not the exception.

display-xl.use: Onboarding statements. One per screen, and it should be hard to ignore.

mono-xs.use: Week numbers. The smallest text in the app, and still legible.

space._note: 4pt base grid. The irregular offsets in the hoard come from the layout, not from off-grid values.

radius._note: 24px and down. The radius dropped with the canvas: on paper, rounded corners stop reading as friendly and start reading as deliberate. A cull is a decision, not a greeting.

glass._note: Four levels, but on paper they are not frosted: they are stacked sheets. A translucent fill is right on glass and wrong on cream, so the levels here are opacity and border, which is what actually reads as depth.

shadow._note: Warm, not neutral. A black shadow on cream reads as dirt; a brown one reads as the card lifting. Low, soft, and never more than two layers.

motion._note: Three tiers, because gravity needs numbers. Anything longer than 520ms feels like the app is broken. Every duration has a matching reduced-motion value, and design_test.go asserts the pairing.

settle.use: Cards entering, sheet present, the ScoreDial count-up.

dramatic.use: The loud moment. Used when the app has earned it.

standard.use: Everything that moves in and out of a place.

emphasized.use: Values that settle: the dial, the wash.

accelerate.use: Exits. Getting out of the way should feel quick.

springSoft.use: The one overshoot in the app. Used once per screen, maximum.

reducedMotion.use: When prefers-reduced-motion is set: zero duration, no drift, no count-up. The score still renders, immediately.

grain._note: Paper texture over everything. Generated, not shipped as a binary: design/grain.go writes a 128px tile so the source is reviewable and the weight is tunable.

blob._note: Washes, not blobs. Four pale seeds that drift behind the content. They exist to keep a large cream field from looking like an empty document, and they must never be strong enough to read as decoration.
